phrase: compre 3 docenas de facturas a 12 mil la docena
note: "la docena" pins the price per pack: 3 x 12.000 = 36.000; verified natural for a bakery restock.

phrase: vendi 12 empanadas a 1500 c/u
note: Typed shorthand "c/u" is an unambiguous per-unit marker: 12 x 1.500 = 18.000.

phrase: vendi 5 tortas a 8000
note: Bare "a" after a count carries both readings (8.000 each = 40.000, or 8.000 the lot); no amount is safe to store.

phrase: me lleve 2 kilos de milanesa a 12.500 el kilo
note: "el kilo" ties the price to the weight unit and the dot is a thousands separator: 2 x 12.500 = 25.000.

phrase: compré dos bolsas de harina a 22.500 la bolsa
note: Spelled-out quantity plus "la bolsa" as per-unit marker: 2 x 22.500 = 45.000.

phrase: a 14 mil el kilo me lleve 3 kilos de asado
note: Price fronted before the quantity (a real topicalization at the carniceria); "el kilo" still marks per-unit: 3 x 14.000 = 42.000.

phrase: vendi 3 pares de medias por 5000
note: Corrected: bare "por" prices the lot in Rioplatense (per-unit needs "cada"), so 5.000 is the total and there is no genuine second reading.

phrase: cargue 25 litros a 1.480 el litro
note: Fuel by volume, "el litro" is per-unit: 25 x 1.480 = 37.000.

phrase: le vendí 100 empanadas a 1200 la unidad
note: "la unidad" is a distinct per-unit token from "c/u": 100 x 1.200 = 120.000.

phrase: compre 10 maples de huevos 8 mil por unidad
note: No preposition before the amount, but "por unidad" resolves it: 10 x 8.000 = 80.000.

phrase: compre 2 sillas de plastico 45 mil
note: Count and amount juxtaposed with no marker: 45.000 each (90.000) or 45.000 for the pair; the app must ask.
known_conflict: Marked ambiguous, while "10 bolsas de cemento 145 mil" (same shape: a count, then an amount, nothing joining them) is marked a total. No rule satisfies both. The parser reads the amount next to a count as the total, which is right far more often and avoids a question on almost every sentence; this case is kept and reported as a known conflict instead of being deleted.

phrase: cobre 3 changas a 50 lucas
note: Same bare-"a" ambiguity applied to counted services: 50.000 per changa (150.000) or 50.000 for all three.

phrase: compre kilo y medio de jamon crudo a 18 mil el kilo
note: Fractional quantity spoken as "kilo y medio" = 1,5; 1,5 x 18.000 = 27.000.

phrase: vendi veinte docenas de facturas a quince mil la docena
note: Dictation with quantity and price both as words (a distinct parsing path); "la docena" is per-pack: 20 x 15.000 = 300.000.

phrase: hice 5 destapaciones a 35 lucas cada una
note: Income cued by "hice" rather than a sale verb; luca = 1.000 and "cada una" forces per-unit: 5 x 35.000 = 175.000.

phrase: me llevé 200 vasos descartables por 60 mil en total
note: "en total" blocks the per-unit reading; store 60.000 and leave unit_price null even though 300 each is derivable.

phrase: 3 tarros de pintura latex 32 lucas el tarro
note: Verbless typed note; "el tarro" is the per-unit marker and luca = 1.000: 3 x 32.000 = 96.000.

phrase: gaste 15 lucas en la verduleria
note: 1 luca = 1.000, so 15 lucas = 15.000. Typed without accents; one amount.

phrase: me pagaron 2 palos por el techo
note: palo = 1.000.000, 2 palos = 2.000.000; 'me pagaron' marca entrada.

phrase: compre 3 cajas de tornillos a 2 lucas cada una
note: "cada una" fixes the unit price at 2.000: 3 x 2.000 = 6.000.

phrase: puse 20k de nafta
note: "k" stuck to the number means thousand. Buying fuel is an expense.

phrase: el flete me salio una fortuna
note: "una fortuna" is emphasis, not an amount: there is no money to store and only one reading.

phrase: vendi 5 docenas de facturas a 6 lucas
note: "a 6 lucas" can be per dozen (30.000) or for the whole sale; the app asks instead of choosing.

phrase: el arreglo de la camioneta me salio un palo y medio
note: "y medio" on "palo" = 1.500.000. Corrected: "la camioneta" became "el arreglo de la camioneta", because no pickup costs 1,5 palos and the case was not realistic.

phrase: le pague 30 lucas y pico al gasista
note: "y pico" is a small, unknown remainder: one reading, and the known floor of 30.000 is stored.

phrase: me cobraron dos mangos por el arreglo
note: Dictionary trap: "dos mangos" means next to nothing, not 2 pesos. No native speaker reads it literally, so it is not ambiguous: it has no amount.

phrase: cobre dos mil quinientos por el delivery
note: Number in full words, typical of voice dictation; "cobre" is income.

phrase: vino la luz 87.430,25
note: Local format (dot for thousands, comma for decimals) with no expense verb: "vino la luz" is the electricity bill arriving.

phrase: el estacionamiento me salio 25 gambas
note: gamba = 100, so 25 gambas = 2.500. Corrected from 5 to 25 gambas, because 500 pesos of parking does not exist and nobody would say the original.

phrase: me deposito el cliente 250 mil pesos
note: Digits + "mil" + a currency word; a customer deposit is income.

phrase: compre 2 bolsas de harina a 18500 c/u
note: "c/u" settles the unit price: 2 x 18.500 = 37.000.

phrase: 20 lucas la caja de vino, lleve 6
note: Inverted order (unit price first, quantity after): 6 x 20.000 = 120.000.

phrase: cobré medio palo por el mural
note: "medio palo" = 500.000, with no number in front.

phrase: gaste $45 mil en insumos
note: Peso sign + digits + the word "mil" in one amount.

phrase: los alfajores salieron 4 lucas y monedas
note: "y monedas" is a small remainder in pesos (not cents) and comes after the amount. Corrected: the phrase was reordered and the note fixed; the floor of 4.000 is stored.

phrase: eh gaste veinte no pera treinta mil en nafta
note: A spoken self-correction ("no, pará"): the later figure counts, 30.000; the earlier one is dropped.

phrase: compre tres bolsas de harina a ocho mil cada una
note: "cada una" fixes the price per bag: 3 x 8.000 = 24.000.

phrase: vendi cinco tortas a ocho mil
note: Without "cada una" there is no telling whether 8.000 is per cake (40.000) or the total; the app asks.

phrase: a ver pague la luz veintitres mil quinientos
note: A filler opening and the amount right after the object with no preposition: 23.500.

phrase: cobre dos palos y medio por el laburo de la cocina
note: "palo" = 1.000.000 plus "y medio" = 2.500.000 of income.

phrase: gaste sesenta 1000 en el mayorista
note: The transcriber wrote "mil" as 1000 inside the spoken number: 60.000.

phrase: puse ciento cincuenta lucas de nafta en la camioneta
note: "luca" = 1.000 and "puse" fuel is an expense: 150.000.

phrase: veinticinco mil de la verduleria
note: The amount is clear (25.000), but with no verb the direction depends on the user's trade: buying at the greengrocer or charging the greengrocer.

phrase: me entraron trescientos cincuenta y siete mil ochocientos de la transferencia
note: "me entraron" marks income; a long number in words: 357.800.

phrase: salieron cuatro mil quinientos cada uno y me lleve seis
note: Inverted order: unit price before the quantity, 6 x 4.500 = 27.000.

phrase: compre dos cajas de doce gaseosas a mil doscientos cada una
note: "cada una" can point at the box (2 x 1.200 = 2.400) or at the bottle (24 x 1.200 = 28.800); the app has to ask.

phrase: che eh no se si lo anote gaste cuarenta y cinco mil quinientos en la ferreteria
note: A long preamble with a distracting clause and no figures; the useful amount is 45.500.

phrase: vendi el sillon en un palo y pico
note: "y pico" leaves the remainder over the million open: there is no exact amount to store.

phrase: eh sali a comprar y gaste ochenta mil en el mayorista y otros quince mil en el chino
note: Two definite expenses (80.000 + 15.000 = 95.000): a native speaker reads it one way. Whether it is stored as one movement or two is an app decision, not an ambiguity of the sentence.

phrase: cobre veinte mil pesos por el arreglo del termotanque
note: No accent on "cobre", but "por el arreglo" confirms 20.000 of income.

phrase: pera no me acuerdo cuanto salio el flete lo tengo que preguntar
note: An expense stated with no figure anywhere in the sentence: there is no amount to store.

phrase: me depositaron un millon doscientos de la factura de julio
note: In Rioplatense Spanish "un millon doscientos" is 1.200.000, never 1.000.200.

phrase: vendi tres docenas de empanadas a mil quinientos la unidad
note: "docena" multiplies by 12 and "la unidad" fixes the price per empanada: 36 x 1.500 = 54.000.

phrase: eh pague la mitad ahora fueron ciento veinte mil y el resto la semana que viene
note: Only what was paid today is recorded, 120.000; the balance due later has no figure.

phrase: cobre 45 lucas por el arreglo del baño
note: luca = 1.000, so 45 lucas = 45.000; "cobre" is money coming in.

phrase: me pagaron 3 fletes a 25 lucas
note: "a 25 lucas" without "cada uno" can be per trip (75.000) or the total for three (25.000); the app asks.

phrase: vendi 3 docenas de facturas a 8500 cada una
note: "cada una" fixes the price per dozen (8.500 a dozen is a real price, per pastry would be absurd): 3 x 8.500 = 25.500.

phrase: vendí 2 kilos de queso a 9.800 el kilo
note: "el kilo" marks the unit price and the dot in 9.800 is a thousands separator: 2 x 9.800 = 19.600.

phrase: entro 200 mil de la venta de la mañana
note: "entro" as an income verb; one explicit amount.

phrase: cierre del dia 1.240.700
note: A verbless end-of-day note; two thousands separators on the million scale: 1.240.700.

phrase: me transfirieron un palo y medio por la cocina
note: palo = 1.000.000 and "y medio" adds half: 1.500.000.

phrase: me depositaron el adelanto, 250k
note: A typed "k" is thousand; a down payment already deposited is money that came in.

phrase: facture 2 melones este mes
note: melon = 1.000.000; the 2 multiplies the money unit, it does not count items, so quantity stays null.

phrase: cobre veinticinco mil quinientos por el service
note: Voice dictation with the number in words: veinticinco mil quinientos = 25.500.

phrase: cobre 100 lucas y pico por la instalacion
note: "y pico" is an unquantified remainder; the known floor, 100.000, is stored.

phrase: me pagaron 50 mil de los 120 que me debian
note: Two numbers, but only 50.000 moved; the 120 mil is the debt it belongs to.

phrase: me dejaron 30 mil de seña
note: The deposit is already collected even though the job is not done: 30.000 comes in.

phrase: me devolvieron 15 mil del pedido que no llego
note: The money comes in, so kind is income. That it is a refund and not a sale is a later classification and does not change the direction.

phrase: me prestaron 500 mil para la heladera
note: Corrected note: money comes in, so kind is income by the direction of the money. That it is a loan is accounting; the original note contradicted its own field.

phrase: le pague 60 mil al gasista
note: Trap: "pague" looks like "me pagaron" but the money goes out. kind corrected from income to expense.

phrase: me cobraron 8500 de comision en mercado pago
note: Trap: "me cobraron" is money going out (a commission taken). kind corrected from income to expense.

phrase: el 15 gaste 20 mil en la verduleria
note: The 15 is a day of the month (no "mil" or currency after it); the money is 20 mil = 20000.

phrase: a las 8 pague 4500 de nafta
note: The 8 is an hour ("a las 8"); the amount is the one after the verb: 4500.

phrase: emiti la factura 1234 por 89 mil
note: 1234 is an invoice number (right after "factura"); the money comes after "por": 89 mil = 89000.

phrase: compre por 50 mil con 20% de descuento
note: Corrected: two real readings. 50 mil can be the list price (40000 after the discount) or what was paid with the discount already taken (50000). "con X% de descuento" is not a subtraction operator the way "menos" is. The app has to ask.

phrase: pague 50 lucas menos el 10 de descuento
note: Here "menos" is an explicit subtraction and "el 10" means 10%, not 10 pesos: 50000 - 10% = 45000.

phrase: el 3 de agosto me pagaron 120 lucas del laburo de palermo
note: 3 is the day of an explicit date ("de agosto"); 120 lucas = 120000 come in.

phrase: cobre 35 mil por el trabajo en rivadavia 2350
note: 2350 is a street number (after a street name); the money is 35 mil.

phrase: vino la boleta de luz con 320 kw, 18.750,40
note: 320 carries a consumption unit (kw); the amount in local format 18.750,40 = 18750.40. The only case with cents, kept for that reason despite the contrived "con 320 kw".

phrase: cargue 20 litros de gasoil, 18500
note: 20 goes with a volume unit; the loose number after the comma reads as the total. As a price per litre (370000) it would be absurd, so there is no real ambiguity.

phrase: pedido 88 lo cobre 12.500
note: 88 is an order number; 12.500 with a thousands dot is 12500 coming in.

phrase: el 10 vendi 4 a 15 mil
note: 10 is the day and 4 the quantity; 15 mil can be per unit (60000) or the whole sale. The parser asks instead of guessing.

phrase: el cliente del 1122334455 me transfirio 80 mil
note: 1122334455 is a phone number (ten digits, no separators, no currency mark); the money is 80 mil.

phrase: lo saque en 3 cuotas de 25 mil
note: "cuotas de X" fixes the value per instalment: 3 x 25000 = 75000 is what the purchase costs.

phrase: facture 100 mil mas iva
note: The amount to store is open: 100000 net or 121000 invoiced. The user chooses.

phrase: hice 120 km de flete y cobre 45 mil
note: 120 carries a distance unit (km); 45 mil come in for the freight.

phrase: 10 bolsas de cemento 145 mil
note: 10 is the number of bags; the amount stands alone, with no "a" or "cada una", so it reads as the total (14.500 a bag, a realistic price; per unit it would be 1.450.000, which is impossible).

phrase: pague 25 mil por 3 kilos de peceto
note: 3 is a weight, not countable units; "por 3 kilos" marks the total paid: 25000. quantity is null because no items are counted.

phrase: vendi 2 docenas a 6 lucas la docena
note: "docena" carries an implicit 12 that is not money; "la docena" fixes the unit price: 2 x 6000 = 12000.

phrase: ayer gaste 15 mil en la verduleria
note: Typed without accents; "ayer" is a date and the only amount is 15 mil = 15000.

phrase: anteayer cobre 120 lucas del laburo de plomeria
note: "cobre" marks income; 120 lucas = 120 x 1000 = 120000.

phrase: el 15 me pagaron 15 mil
note: A repeated number: the first 15 is the day of the month, the second carries "mil" and is the amount.

phrase: el jueves 12 gaste 12 lucas en insumos
note: "jueves 12" is a date (weekday + number); only the 12 next to "lucas" is money.

phrase: El 3 de agosto cobre 250 mil de la obra
note: A full date that opens with a number; the amount is 250 mil = 250000.

phrase: el 20 de junio me depositaron 1.250.500 por la obra del centro
note: Argentine thousands dots: 1.250.500 pesos; the 20 is a date, not money.

phrase: hoy temprano puse 30 lucas de nafta
note: "puse ... de nafta" is money going out; 30 lucas = 30000.

phrase: recien pague 8500 de la boleta del gas
note: "recien" is a time marker with no number; the amount is in plain digits.

phrase: a principios de mes pague el alquiler, 320 mil
note: A vague date with no number at all; the amount comes after the comma.

phrase: el martes pasado vendi 3 tortas a 8000 cada una
note: "cada una" settles the unit price: 3 x 8000 = 24000.

phrase: la semana pasada compre 20 kilos de harina a 1200 el kilo
note: "el kilo" marks the price per unit: 20 x 1200 = 24000.

phrase: el viernes vendi 5 docenas a 12 mil
note: Without "cada una" or "todo", 12 mil can be per dozen (60000) or the whole sale; the parser asks instead of guessing.

phrase: ayer compre 6 cajones de tomate, 45 lucas todo
note: "todo" settles that 45 lucas is the total; the price per crate is not stated, so unit_price stays null.

phrase: hace dos dias le pague 80 mil al pintor
note: "dos" is part of a date written in words: neither a count of items nor money.

phrase: el jeuves pague 22 lucas de luz
note: A common keyboard typo in "jueves"; the misspelled date does not touch the amount of 22000.

phrase: el mes pasado se me fueron como 200 mil en fletes
note: "como" approximates, it does not offer two readings: there is one determinable amount, 200000.

phrase: el finde pasado gaste 32.500,50 en el super
note: A number copied from a till receipt: Argentine thousands dot and decimal comma = 32500 and 50 cents.

phrase: el martes pague la boleta del agua pero no me acuerdo cuanto
note: There is a date and a clear direction but no amount: total is null for lack of data, not for ambiguity.

phrase: manana pago 40 mil de monotributo
note: Future tense: amount 40000, date tomorrow. The money has not left yet, but the direction is expense.

phrase: anoche cobre 2 palos y medio por la camioneta
note: "2 palos y medio" = 2,5 x 1.000.000 = 2500000; "anoche" is the date.

phrase: pague 5 mil de luz y 3 mil de gas
note: Two expenses joined by "y": 5.000 + 3.000 = 8.000. If the app splits the record in two, the sum is the same.

phrase: gaste 12.500 en internet y 8.300 en el cable
note: Argentine thousands dot (not a decimal point): 12.500 + 8.300 = 20.800.

phrase: 15 mil mas 2 mil de envio
note: A verbless note, a base amount plus a surcharge joined by "mas": 15.000 + 2.000 = 17.000.

phrase: compre 3 bolsas de cemento a 9500 cada una mas 4 mil de flete
note: "cada una" fixes the unit price: 3 x 9.500 = 28.500, and the 4.000 freight is added on top, so total != quantity x unit price.

phrase: como 20 mil en la verduleria
note: "como" approximates (and is a trap with the verb "comer"), it is not uncertainty between two figures: 20.000 is stored.

phrase: unos 15 lucas de nafta
note: "unos" rounds and luca = 1.000: 15.000.

phrase: entre 20 y 25 mil de flete
note: A real range: neither averaging nor keeping one end. The app asks for the amount.

phrase: me dijeron q sale 40 o 50 mil
note: Two alternative figures, and it is a quote, not a payment made: ask again before storing.

phrase: compre la heladera en 6 cuotas sin interes de 25 lucas
note: Corrected: there was a total of 150.000, but the case was already marked ambiguous. The two readings (the full price 6 x 25.000 = 150.000, or the 25.000 instalment that leaves today) stay in quantity and unit_price; the total is not resolved.

phrase: cobre 50 mil de la obra y pague 12 mil de materiales
note: Income and expense in the same sentence: they are not added and do not fit one record with a single kind (the income kind is a schema placeholder).

phrase: me pagaron 100 mil pero me descontaron 10 mil de comision
note: Gross 100.000 or net 90.000 depending on how the books are kept: the app asks instead of choosing.

phrase: vendi 2 docenas de facturas a 9 mil la docena y 1500 de envio
note: "la docena" anchors the unit price and removes the usual ambiguity of "vendi 2 a 9 mil": 2 x 9.000 = 18.000 + 1.500 of delivery charged = 19.500.

phrase: cargue treinta lucas de nafta y cinco mil de peaje
note: Dictation with numbers in words: 30.000 + 5.000 = 35.000.

phrase: pague la mitad de los 80 mil del alquiler
note: "la mitad" is a closed fraction, not a range: what left is 40.000; the 80.000 is the debt, not the movement.

phrase: compre mercaderia en el mayorista
note: A clear movement and direction but no figure: total is null and the app asks for the amount.

phrase: hola buen dia
note: A greeting typical of a chat channel: no movement and no amount, it must not create a record (the kind is a schema placeholder).

phrase: cuanto gaste este mes?
note: A question that contains the expense verb: a classic trap. It has to be answered, not stored.

phrase: se me fueron 30 y pico de lucas en el chino
note: "30 y pico de lucas" is "30 lucas y pico" said in the other order, and the corpus already fixed that reading at 30.000 with approximate. A bare "lucas" is not one thousand: it is the scale of the number in front of it. The earlier parser returned 1.000.

phrase: me salio 40 y pico de lucas el service
note: Same shape, different verb. The earlier parser returned the same 1.000 whatever the number was, and 1.000 is a plausible amount, so nothing downstream caught it.

phrase: me salio cuarenta y pico de lucas el arreglo
note: The count spelled out. It has to fold the same way as the digits, or the transcription of a spoken sentence parses differently from the typed one.

phrase: me salio 40 y pico mil el remis
note: Without the "de". The scale word is still the scale of the 40, not a number of its own.

phrase: el arreglo me salio un par de lucas
note: "un par de lucas" is two thousand: "par" is the count and "lucas" the scale. The earlier parser dropped the count and stored half.

phrase: el arreglo me salio un par de palos
note: The same defect on the million scale, where it is worth a million pesos.

phrase: deje mil pesos de propina
note: CONTROL. A scale word with nothing in front of it really is one thousand when it opens the amount. The fix must only reach back to a number that is actually there.

phrase: compre un par de zapatillas 45 mil
note: CONTROL. "un par de" followed by a thing, not a scale, counts shoes and does not touch the price.

phrase: pague la luz 45 mil, el gas 12 mil
note: A comma is what a voice transcription writes when somebody lists. The same sentence with "y" already returned 57.000, so reading the comma any other way made the parser disagree with itself. The earlier parser kept the first figure and dropped the second with no flag.

phrase: compre 20 mil de verdura, 15 mil de carne
note: Two purchases in one breath. What left the till is the sum, exactly as with "y".

phrase: cobre 80 mil, me quedan 20 mil
note: CONTROL. The comma joins, but "quedan" says the second figure is what is left in the till, not part of what came in. The not-the-movement words have to work across a comma exactly as they do across "y".

phrase: vendi la camioneta en 20 mil dolares
note: The parser has no currency field: the caller stamps one fixed currency on whatever comes back, so the earlier parser had this stored and shown as twenty thousand pesos. The figure is readable; what cannot be done is store it. A peso number is the one answer that is certainly wrong.

phrase: pague 15 mil dolares de la maquina nueva
note: Same cause on the expense side. A cross-check with a language model does not catch it either: asked for the total in the local currency while reading the same fragment, the model agrees.

phrase: u$s 200 de sena
note: The symbol, which the tokenizer splits into three pieces. The earlier parser returned exactly what it returns for "$ 200 de sena".

phrase: me pagaron 800 usd por el trabajo
note: The earlier parser already returned nothing here, but by accident: "usd" read as a countable noun and the 800 became a quantity. An accident is not a rule; the same sentence with "dolares" returned the figure.

phrase: vendi la camioneta en 20 mil
note: CONTROL. Without the currency word it is pesos and an ordinary sale.

phrase: compre el horno en 18 cuotas fijas de 40 mil
note: The earlier rule demanded that "de" sit exactly two tokens after the count, so one adjective switched it off and the purchase was stored at one eighteenth. "Cuotas fijas" is how financing is actually spoken.

phrase: compre el horno en 18 cuotas mensuales de 40 mil
note: The other adjective that shows up in the same slot.

phrase: el proveedor me lo financia en 4 pagos de 90 mil
note: The synonym a supplier uses. Same shape as "3 cuotas de 25 mil", which already computed: the machinery existed, the word was missing.

phrase: me lo financian en 6 pagos mensuales de 30 mil
note: Synonym and adjective together, which is how it is usually said.

phrase: lo compre en 12 sin interes de 8000
note: "12 sin interes" is a fixed phrase, and dropping the word "cuotas" turned off a question the corpus already asks ("6 cuotas sin interes de 25 lucas"). Worse than a wrong total: the earlier parser answered 12, twelve pesos, because the count tied the price on score and won on position.

phrase: me lo dieron en 3 cuotas de 20 mil mas un anticipo de 50 mil
note: Nothing is ambiguous: three instalments of 20.000 plus a 50.000 down payment, joined by the same connector the parser adds with everywhere else. The instalments branch returned before that rule, so the earlier parser lost the down payment whole. quantity and unit_price describe the instalments; the extra is on top, as in the unit-price branch.

phrase: pague la tele 300 mil en 3 cuotas
note: CONTROL. The total is named and then how it was financed. Multiplying here turns 300.000 into 900.000, which is why only the amount that follows "cuotas de" may be multiplied. Letting an adjective through must not loosen that.

phrase: lo pago en 3 cuotas de 40 mil a partir de marzo
note: CONTROL. "de 40 mil a partir" is not a range: what follows the "a" is a date, not a second figure.

phrase: el gasista me pidio de 80 mil a 100 mil
note: A range is not a number, and the parser already knew it: "entre 20 y 25 mil" asks. With this preposition the earlier parser answered 80.000 without asking, picking the low end of two readings it considered unresolvable when they arrive with the other word.

phrase: me presupuestaron de 200 mil a 250 mil
note: A quote given as a range is as common as the "entre" form.

phrase: sale de 15 lucas a 20 lucas
note: The same shape in slang, to make sure the rule reads the folded number and not the digits.

phrase: el proveedor me cobro 200 mil mas el 21 de iva
note: The same sentence without "el 21 de" already asked. Naming the rate is how a supplier says it, and it slipped past because the rule wanted "mas" and "iva" side by side. The 21 is swallowed by the date rule on the way, so it is not even a candidate.

phrase: me facturo 500 mil con el 21 de iva
note: The other preposition, same question: net or invoiced.

phrase: pague 60 mil con el iva incluido
note: CONTROL. "iva incluido" states that the figure IS the total. Widening the rule to the bare word must not turn a stated total into a question.

phrase: gaste 80 mil menos el 20%
note: The subtraction is explicit: "menos" is the operator and "el 20%" the rate. The parser already computed exactly this when the noun "descuento" was in the sentence, so whether the discount is applied cannot depend on that noun. In the earlier parser the sentence fell between two rules that cancelled each other and the gross was stored without asking.

phrase: compre por 50 mil menos el 10 por ciento
note: The rate spelled out instead of the sign. Same arithmetic.

phrase: me hicieron un 10 de descuento sobre 45 mil
note: Not computable and not a total either: "un 10" over 45 mil is ten percent for most speakers and ten lucas for plenty of others, and there is no "menos" to make it arithmetic. What is certainly wrong is 45.000, the gross of a sentence whose whole point is that it was discounted.

phrase: el mayorista me hace 10 puntos de descuento sobre 300 mil
note: "Puntos" arguably pins it at 270.000, and a rule could be written for that word. It is not, on purpose: every literal-word branch in this parser is one adjective away from switching off, and this family is the one that proves it. A discount the parser could not apply is a question, not a gross.

phrase: de los 80 mil me devolvieron 20 mil
note: What moved is the 20.000 refunded; the 80 mil is the context it came out of. Opening with "de los X" names a total already spent. The earlier parser stored 80.000: four times too much, on a movement in the opposite direction.

phrase: de los 120 mil que le debia le pague 40 mil
note: The same opening on the expense side. The debt is the context; what left the till is the 40.000.

phrase: me devolvieron 3 remeras de 12 mil
note: The same question as "vendi 5 tortas a 8000", with the other preposition. Most speakers read 12 mil each (36.000) and careless speech reads the lot, so it is the third answer. The unit-or-total rule was written for this exact shape but only looked when the marker was "a".

phrase: saque 4 entradas de 12 mil
note: Four tickets at twelve thousand each is the dominant reading and 12.000 for the lot is not impossible. Either way, 12.000 as a confident answer is the one nobody meant.

phrase: compre 10 bolsas de cemento a 4500 la bolsa
note: CONTROL. A per-unit marker outranks the preposition: this one multiplies and must not become a question. The other control for this family, "10 bolsas de cemento 145 mil", is already in the corpus: a count and an amount with a plain noun between them is the total.
